title: namespace rebind causes transient token under-accounting during policy failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a control-plane-driven namespace rebind (used when routes are remapped across shards for failover), we observed token under-accounting for a subset of per-key requests. The effect is transient free allowance for affected keys (~1–3s), resulting in underbilling and potential quota overuse. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, fix, and rollout for the policy evaluation and enforcement path affected by namespace rebinds.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure two route aliases that map to the same org but different route-shard bindings (route-A -> shard-1, route-B -> shard-2).
2) Load test with steady per-key QPS that consumes tokens within the burst window (use loadtool v0.9 with consistent client key X).
3) Trigger a namespace rebind: move route-B bindings from shard-2 -> shard-1 via the control plane (simulate shard reclaim/failover).
4) Observe telemetry: enforcement logs show a small window where policy-evaluator does not debit per-key token store for requests routed during the rebind handoff.
5) Correlate with billing: aggregated metering shows missing increments for affected keys during the handoff window.
impact: Affected customers may see short bursts of requests that are not charged / accounted for. In worst cases this could allow quota overages and allow callers to exceed rate limits briefly. Estimated magnitude: for a high-traffic org with many routed aliases, under-accounting could total thousands of tokens per minute during a large-scale rebind event.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial report from PG: anomaly spike in 'allowed' events with zero meter increments; observed across multiple regions.
2026-03-11 - Reproduced locally by simulating namespace rebind; attached transient logs from rate_engine (see links below).

2026-03-12 - Root-cause hypothesis: duplicate ephemeral namespace objects cause one enforce path to short-circuit debit if it sees a 'pending-rebind' marker and defers to the control-plane reconciler. Race reproduces with ~10% probability under load.

2026-03-13 - Adding additional tracing shows sequence: request -> policy-eval -> check namespace_vsn(42) vs current_vsn(43) -> path chooses fallback fast-allow and schedules background debit to reconciler, but background debit sometimes lost when ephemeral namespace object is GC'd early.
2026-03-14 - Confirmed missing KV writes in meter-store for the background debit path due to a short TTL on ephemeral keys created by the rebind handler.
root_cause: During namespace rebind, the rebind handler creates ephemeral mapping tokens to bridge in-flight requests. A fast-path optimization allowed the policy evaluator to avoid synchronous debits by scheduling an asynchronous 'reconcile debit' using ephemeral keys with a short TTL. Under high QPS and tight GC timing, the ephemeral keys were garbage-collected before the reconcile debit could persist to the meter-store, causing permanent loss of the debit increments.
proposed_fix: 1) Disable the fast-path asynchronous debit for per-key quota enforcement during rebinds — fall back to synchronous debit until a safe handoff is confirmed.
2) Extend TTL and make ephemeral keys idempotent (use a unique request nonce + write-ahead log) so background debits can be replayed after GC.
3) Add a control-plane handshake that marks a rebind as 'handoff-complete' only after all pending reconcile debits are confirmed persisted.
4) Add feature flag 'rebind-sync-accounting' to gate the change and allow gradual rollout.
5) Add end-to-end tests to exercise rebind handoff under contention.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Enable 'rebind-sync-accounting' on 5% of runtime hosts in eu-west-1. Monitor token accounting mismatch metric and error rates. (owner: Jonah)
Stage 2 (regional): Expand to 25% of hosts and enable extended tracing for rebinds (owner: Jonah + SRE)
Stage 3 (global): Flip feature flag globally if metrics stable for 48h; then deploy TTL/idempotency improvements and remove feature flag after 1 week of stability.
Rollback: Immediately revert to previous runtime image or disable feature flag if accounting mismatch increases or latency regression > 5% on p95.
tests: Unit: Add tests for policy_evaluator to assert synchronous debit path during rebind flag.
Integration: Simulate namespace rebind under synthetic load with deterministic GC timing to assert no missing meter-store writes.
E2E: Regression harness that runs nightly for 7 days with realistic traffic shape and rebind events.
